Based on my search, I found one potentially related PR:

**PR #9365: feat(session): add support for per-session working directories**
https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/9365

**Why it might be related:** This PR also addresses working directory management, though it appears to be focused on per-session working directory support rather than runtime switching via a slash command. It could represent a different approach to the same underlying feature.

Note: PR #16167 "feat(opencode): add /cd to cli prompt" also appeared in search results, but this seems to be a CLI feature rather than TUI-specific, so it may be tangentially related or a different implementation context.

The current PR (23360) is a focused reimplementation of a previous attempt (#7266) with a much smaller footprint, as mentioned in the description.

A couple of notes for context:

1. This implementation was built using OpenCode itself (powered by claude-opus-4-6) — dogfooding OpenCode to enhance OpenCode.

2. My primary use case: I frequently switch between git worktrees mid-session. The workflow is to start a new session, use shell mode to run `git worktree add`, and then `/cd` into the new worktree directory. The built-in `!cd` shell command doesn't actually change OpenCode's working directory (it only affects the spawned shell subprocess), so `/cd` fills a real gap here.

One more detail on the UX: when you run `/cd <path>`, it shows up in the session as a shell command `$ cd <path>` (with `pwd` output showing the new directory), so it looks and feels consistent with regular shell commands — but unlike `!cd`, it actually changes OpenCode's working directory for all subsequent operations.

This issue might be a duplicate of an existing issue. Please check:
- #22650: Same root cause — `formatPatch(structuredPatch(..., { context: Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER }))` blocking the main thread causing UI lag/freeze in the diff pipeline. That issue also covers `SessionSummary` and `snapshot/index.ts` as bottlenecks.

This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #23315: no release for version 1.4.12 — same missing releases issue
- #23348: Release v1.4.12 assets missing — Homebrew tap upgrade fails with 404 — same skipped/missing release issue
- #23350: brew error — same missing release assets causing 404 errors
Closing as duplicate of #22650 — same root cause (`formatPatch(structuredPatch(..., { context: Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER }))` in `snapshot/index.ts`). Adding our findings as a comment on #22650.

Additional findings from a TUI-side investigation (originally #23362):

- **Regression commit**: `b7fab49b6` — *refactor(snapshot): store unified patches in file diffs (#21244)*. Parent `463318486` is the last good commit. Identified via `git bisect` (9 steps between `v1.3.3` and HEAD).
- **TUI manifestation**: On TUI, this causes a **complete freeze** (not just lag) — `strace` confirms all threads end up in `FUTEX_WAIT`, 0% CPU. ESC and all input become unresponsive.
- **Trigger path**: `SessionSummary.summarize()` fire-and-forget call in `prompt.ts` → `computeDiff` → `snapshot.diffFull()` → `formatPatch(structuredPatch(...))` blocks the event loop.
- **Tested fix**: Replacing `formatPatch(structuredPatch(...))` with `git diff --no-ext-diff --no-renames` subprocess eliminates the hang. Non-blocking, faster, equivalent output.

Still reproducing on my side with nested subagent navigation:
1. enter first child with Ctrl+X, Down
2. from there, create another child
3. Ctrl+X, Down no longer descends into the sub-subagent

The bug came from computing child navigation relative to the wrong session level
once you were inside a child session, OpenCode was effectively looking at the parent level again
so Ctrl+X, Down could no longer find the current child’s own children

The fix:
computes visible child navigation from the current session id
picks the first direct child of the current session when descending
keeps sibling cycling scoped to the current depth

So after the fix:
parent -> child still works
child -> sub-child now also works
sibling navigation stays at the right level instead of mixing levels

> I encountered the same issue. here is my workaround.
> 
> Workaround that fixed it for me without any code change — just config.
> Drop this into `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` (global) to bind `Ctrl+X V` as a fallback for `Ctrl+V`:
> ```json
> {
>   "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
>   "keybinds": {
>     "input_paste": "ctrl+v,<leader>v"
>   }
> }
> ```
> 
> Default leader is Ctrl+X, so Ctrl+X then V triggers the same paste path. Because V arrives as a regular keypress after Ctrl+X, the terminal has no reason to intercept it, which bypasses whatever swallows Ctrl+V.
> 
> Environment where this was confirmed working:
> - opencode: 1.4.11
> - Windows Terminal on Windows 11: 1.24.10921.0
> - WSL: Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS on WSL2 (kernel 6.6.87.2)
